rows.rule: Dark Pacts trigger on being selected to shoot, with no phase named. The out-of-phase rule only bars rules that trigger in the Shooting phase itself. Community rulings (B&C, Ruleshammer) let a Pact be made on Overwatch. No official FAQ settles it.
rows.source: wahapedia zarkan-s-daemonkin; Rules Commentary 'Out-of-phase rules'; bolterandchainsword topic 382706
rows.fix: Owner decision. Recommend allowing the Pact on Overwatch: open shooting.unitSelected for Overwatch shooters in movement.ts and charge.ts (only darkPact and sacrificialDagger picks), and drop CHA-2.4 / CHA-009.

rows.rule: Dark Pact: take a Leadership test (2D6 >= best Ld; not a Battle-shock test). A fail deals D3 mortal wounds, and the chosen ability applies whether the test passes or fails. Every datasheet, Cultist Mob included, has Dark Pacts.

The Leadership test and any mortal wounds come first, when the unit is selected and before it attacks. Resolving them before targets are declared is equivalent. Pact and Dagger order is the owner's choice.
Stratagems that say 'the Fight phase' (not 'your') can be used in either player's Fight phase. Vindictive Strategy reads 'your Shooting phase or the Fight phase'.
Sites of Power: from round 2, at the end of your turn, score 2VP if you control at least as many objective markers as the opponent. A 0 v 0 tie scores under the literal reading.

Re-checked, the deviation holds. Marked for Execution scores 12VP if the opponent's WARLORD is destroyed in rounds 1-3 and 6VP after that. It does not say 'by you', so the Rules Commentary 'Destroyed By' limit does not apply. The CP rules say a Reserves unit that has not arrived by the end of round 3 counts as destroyed, along with anything embarked in it. A stranded Warlord should therefore score 12VP in round 3. missions.ts says outright that it does not score, and cullStrandedReserves never calls the missions unitDestroyed hook.
rows.source: wahapedia zarkan-s-daemonkin (Marked for Execution); wahapedia CP rules step 5 Reserves; Rules Commentary 'Destroyed By'; src/engine/phases/movement.ts cullStrandedReserves; src/engine/missions.ts markedForExecutionDestroyed
rows.fix: In movement.ts destroyStrandedUnit, after the UnitDestroyed emit, call ctx.services.missions.unitDestroyed?.(ctx, { unitId, byPlayer: null, byUnitId: null, byModelId: null }). This matches teleport.ts:118. Treasures and Hallowed Retribution already ignore a null byPlayer. Rewrite the missions.ts comment and the CHA-4 spec line, and add a CHA test: Warlord stranded in Reserves gives 12VP at the end of round 3.

rows.rule: Zarkan can attach to Legionaries or Possessed. Attaching to Possessed by default is a legal choice.
Zarkan's core abilities have no Deep Strike. Legionaries and Cultist Mob have no Patrol Squads in this patrol.

Re-checked, the deviation holds. The Rules Commentary 'Fight on Death' says the destroyed model fights through the normal sequence: it may Pile In (keeping Unit Coherency), then picks weapons and targets and attacks. It counts as having 1 wound, and this all happens before the attacking unit Consolidates. It then does not Consolidate. resolveDeferredDeaths goes straight to declareTargets with no pile-in. The commentary does not say whether the model is 'selected to fight', so keeping it out of selection triggers is still our interpretation.
rows.source: Rules Commentary 'Fight on Death'; wahapedia zarkan-s-daemonkin (Daemonic Fervour); src/engine/fight-on-death.ts
rows.fix: In fight-on-death.ts resolveDeferredDeaths, offer an optional pile-in of up to 3 inches for the deferred models of each unit before declareTargets. Reuse the fight.ts pile-in validation, limited to those models, with coherency checked against the unit's living models. Keep the existing order (before doConsolidate), no consolidate, and no Pact/Dagger. Add a CHA test where a deferred model piles in and then attacks.

rows.rule: Re-checked, the deviation holds as part of CSM-09. Because the published sequence allows a pile-in, a deferred model that starts out of Engagement Range is not automatically out of the fight. Eligibility to attack should follow the normal rule after the pile-in: within Engagement Range, or in base contact with a friendly model that is in base contact with an enemy. The engine checks Engagement Range only, before any move. The mirror-match chain (deferred models killing enemy deferred models) is not covered by the published rules.
rows.source: Rules Commentary 'Fight on Death' (normal fight sequence; pile in, then attack); 10-rules-core R-9.6
rows.fix: Fixed with CSM-09: work out the legal targets after the pile-in, using the same eligibility as normal fighting (fight.ts), not ER-only. Keep the any-order drain and the end-of-phase purge, labelled as interpretations.

rows.rule: Violent Unbinding is used just after an attack destroys the model. The request opens once that attack's damage has resolved, before the next attack, which matches the rule.
Range is measured from where Zarkan stood. The queued mortal wounds drain in advance() after the death-reaction window and before the next attack's allocation, so they are effectively immediate.
rows.source: wahapedia Violent Unbinding; attack.ts advance mortalQueue order

rows.rule: Re-checked, the deviation holds. Vindictive Strategy re-rolls a hit roll of 1 against a target below its Starting Strength, and also a wound roll of 1 if the target is Below Half-strength. The Rules Commentary says a unit with Starting Strength 1 is below its Starting Strength once its model has fewer wounds than it started with. The gate uses boardCount < SS || isBelowHalfStrength, so a wounded single model above half wounds gets no hit re-roll. Example: a 5-wound character on 4 wounds.
rows.source: wahapedia zarkan-s-daemonkin (Vindictive Strategy); Rules Commentary 'Below Starting Strength (with a Starting Strength of 1)'; src/engine/factions/chaos-space-marines.ts vindictiveStrategy.gateEffect; src/engine/leaders.ts
rows.fix: In leaders.ts isBelowStartingStrength, when the combined Starting Strength is 1, return true when the model's woundsRemaining is below its W. In chaos-space-marines.ts, make the hit branch call leaderService.isBelowStartingStrength(state, t) and leave the wound branch on isBelowHalfStrength. Then delete boardCount if nothing else uses it. Add a CHA-017 case with a wounded single-model target.

rows.rule: Prey on the Weak picks a unit hit by the bearer's psychic weapon (Rite of Possession, both profiles). Matching on the weapon id or its profile group covers both profiles.

Rules Commentary 'Keywords': an attached unit has the keywords of every model in it, so matching a positive keyword on any half is correct. A notKeyword that excludes when any half has it is consistent with this.
Precision is optional ('can'), so the attacker may decline and use normal allocation. Both modules now hand allocateAttack decisions to attackService.
The prompt describes the 2D6 Leadership test, the D3 mortal wounds on a fail, and that the ability applies on a pass or a fail, all in our own words.
Figures are cosmetic. Bases match the datasheets: Zarkan 40mm, Possessed 40mm, Legionaries 32mm.
The Combat Patrol: Tyranids box matches the Vardenghast Swarm roster (Prime, Psychophage, 20 Termagants, 5 Barbgaunts, 3 Leapers, June 2023). Insidious Infiltrators needs separate kits.

Re-checked, the deviation holds. Death Blow lets the model fight after the attacking unit has finished its attacks. The Rules Commentary 'Fight on Death' adds three things: this happens before the attacker Consolidates, the model may pile in and then attack, and it does not Consolidate. The engine offers Death Blow in doFightSelect, which runs only after the attacker has finished its whole activation (consolidation and the fight.attacksResolved window included). It then runs a full activation: the FightUnitSelected event, pile-in, attacks and consolidate, gated by eligibleToFight measured after the attacker's consolidation. Whether the model is 'selected to fight' is not stated.
rows.source: wahapedia the-vardenghast-swarm (Death Blow); Rules Commentary 'Fight on Death'; src/engine/phases/fight.ts doFightSelect / driveFightUnit
rows.fix: Move Death Blow onto the fight-on-death.ts path, called from driveFightUnit before doConsolidate. Keep the use/decline choice, add the pile-in from CSM-09 and skip consolidate. Do not emit FightUnitSelected or open fight.unitSelected (interpretation). Remove the pendingDeathBlowUnits loop from doFightSelect. Unify Model.pendingRemoval with the deferredDeath marks so allocation and purging use one mechanism. Update TYR-026.

rows.rule: Hyper-Reactive: in the opponent's Shooting phase or either Fight phase, just after an enemy unit selects its targets.

Psychophage: 120x92mm oval base, Deadly Demise 1, Feel No Pain 5+, no PSYKER keyword. Anti-Psyker 4+ only matters against PSYKER targets. The Prime has no Leader ability. FNP stored as 5 is read by attack.ts bestFeelNoPain.
Bearer gets Lone Operative and a 4+ invulnerable save, and melee attacks targeting it take -1 to hit. Merging these into one descriptor is equivalent, and TYR-008 and TYR-009 test it.

Re-checked, the deviation holds. Feeding Frenzy gives +1 to hit on melee attacks against a unit below its Starting Strength, and also +1 to wound if that unit is Below Half-strength. Under the Rules Commentary, a Starting Strength 1 unit is below its Starting Strength once it has lost any wound. hooks-impl targetBelowStartingStrength calls leaderService.isBelowStartingStrength, which only counts models. A wounded single-model target (a monster, vehicle or lone character) above half wounds therefore never gives the +1 to hit.
rows.source: wahapedia the-vardenghast-swarm (Feeding Frenzy); Rules Commentary 'Below Starting Strength (with a Starting Strength of 1)'; src/engine/leaders.ts; src/engine/hooks-impl.ts:230
rows.fix: Fixed by the same leaders.ts isBelowStartingStrength change as CSM-13. The descriptor is fine. Add a TYR-029 case where the Psychophage attacks a wounded single-model target above half wounds and gets +1 to hit but not +1 to wound.

rows.rule: Once per battle, in either player's Command phase, while a unit with the ability is on the battlefield: every enemy unit takes a Battle-shock test. Declining keeps the use. Shock expiry (shockExpiryRound) keeps a failed enemy shocked through its own turn.
rows.source: wahapedia Shadow in the Warp; hooks-impl.ts shockExpiryRound

rows.rule: A TYRANIDS unit within 6 inches of a friendly SYNAPSE model takes Battle-shock tests on 3D6. A SYNAPSE model is within range of itself. Using a separate dice field is implementation only.

Used in your Reinforcements step: return up to D6 destroyed models, or add a 2D6-model copy in Strategic Reserves. Returning the maximum is fine. Nothing says whether the copy can arrive in the same step; the engine waits for a later step, so a round-3 use always gets culled.
rows.source: wahapedia Teeming Broods; Rules Commentary (no entry)
rows.fix: Owner decision. A literal reading allows a same-step arrival: in movement.ts, re-read the Reserves list after the movement.reinforcements window and raise arrivals for new units. AI (round<=2) would then become round<=3. Hiding no-op offers is UI only.

rows.rule: Strategic Reserves (core): from round 2, wholly within 6 inches of a battlefield edge, more than 9 inches horizontally from enemy models, and not in the enemy deployment zone in round 2. A Deep Strike unit may use either method.

Chitinous Tide: at the end of your turn, a flat 5VP if you control one or more markers within 6 inches of the opponent's deployment zone. A marker inside the zone is within 0 inches. Measuring to the edge of the marker follows core.

Re-checked, the deviation holds. Rules Commentary 'Closest Model/Unit': when several units are equally close, the controlling player of the unit using the rule picks which one counts as the closest. closestEligibleTargets returns every tied unit, so Voracious Assault re-rolls attacks into all of them. This has a real effect in melee, where every unit in base contact is at distance 0 and ties are common.
rows.source: Rules Commentary 'Closest Model/Unit'; wahapedia the-vardenghast-swarm (Voracious Assault); src/engine/leaders.ts closestEligibleTargets; src/engine/factions/tyranids.ts snapshotClosestEligible
rows.fix: In tyranids.ts snapshotClosestEligible, keep a single unit when there is a tie. If the declaration targets only one of the tied units, pick that one. If it targets more than one, ask the controlling player with chooseOption. Update TYR-019 and the TYR-5.2 spec line from 'every tied unit counts' to 'player picks one'.

rows.rule: Target: a TYRANIDS unit not yet selected to shoot or fight this phase. notYetShot and notYetFought cover this.
Heroic Intervention may target the Leapers for 0CP, even if it was already used on another unit this phase. Offering it at 0 CP is correct.

In your Shooting phase, after the unit has shot, pick an enemy INFANTRY unit it hit. Auto-hits count as hits. The effect is -2 Move and -2 to Advance and Charge rolls until the end of the opponent's next turn, which is the start of the Tyranid player's next turn.

Once per turn, when a friendly TYRANIDS unit within 6 inches is selected to shoot or fight, its AP improves by 1 for the phase. Offering it at target declaration has the same effect, and declining does not spend it.
rows.fix: none (see TYR-02: Death Blow must stop opening fight.unitSelected)

rows.rule: Re-checked, the deviation holds. Infiltrators may set up anywhere more than 9 inches horizontally from the enemy deployment zone and from all enemy models. On cp-04 the zones are triangles: zone B is (22,-15),(22,15),(0,15). The grown bounding rectangle covers x from -9 to 31, so it forbids almost all of No Man's Land. For example, (0,-12) is about 16 inches from zone B and is legal, but the engine rejects it. The rectangle is exact only for the strip zones in cp-01/02/03/05/06.
rows.source: 10-rules-core R-10.7; wahapedia the-vardenghast-swarm (Von Ryan's Leapers, Infiltrators); src/data/missions/cp-04.json; src/engine/setup.ts infiltratorConstraints; src/client/interaction/formationValidation.ts inInfiltratorArea
rows.fix: In setup.ts infiltratorConstraints, measure against the real zone polygon. A model is legal if it is not inside the polygon and (pointToPolygonEdge from its centre minus its base radius) > 9. If MoveConstraints.forbidden only takes polygons, add a minDistanceFromPolygon field or a buffered polygon instead. Mirror this in the client's formationValidation.ts inInfiltratorArea. Add a cp-04 TYR-037 case where (0,-12) is accepted.

rows.rule: Patrol Squads: split during Declare Battle Formations, before deployment. Each half has Starting Strength 10. Splitting at the start of the deploy step makes no difference here (Termagants have no leader or Reserves option).

The rule checks 'the closest eligible target' at each attack. The published rules don't say whether closeness is fixed when targets are declared or changes as casualties are removed. Fixing it at declaration matches how target legality is fixed.
rows.fix: Keep the snapshot; the owner should confirm. It only matters when a weapon group's casualties change which unit is closest partway through the shooting.

rows.rule: Sound mapping is cosmetic with no rules effect.
